f.h:
Numeric Licensing

Bank Identification Number (BIN) and Acquiring ID Fees

Special numeric fees will be applied for a specific numeric request (i.e., a specific series of numbers or a request for a numeric that has never been issued).

Annual Numeric Licensing Fees

A numeric is considered utilized if the activity threshold is achieved in any month during the 12-month period (1 July through 30 June). Numerics that do not meet the activity threshold in at least one month of the usage period are considered underutilized.

  • Fees for newly assigned numerics will apply 18 months after the BIN is issued.
  • Any eight-digit BINs that have been converted from six-digit BINs will immediately be eligible for annual program fees (e.g., the 18-month start-up grace period will not apply).

Six-digit BINs submitted into the Issuer BIN Migration Tool before 1 August will be billed as eight-digit BINs.

Numerics released prior to the program deadline are not invoiced. Please contact your Visa representative for additional program details.

Monthly Numeric Utilization Program

Important: Immediately following the end of the 2024 annual program, Visa will begin billing fees related to the Annual Numeric Licensing Program on a monthly, rather than annual, basis. At the same time, the program will be renamed the "Numeric Utilization Program," to align more closely with its purpose. 

Note: Distinct pricing previously in place for Proprietary ATM, Private Label and Domestic Use-Only BINs has been removed. All BINs, no matter their use, will be assessed Annual Program fees based solely on their length.

f.h:
Visa B2B Connect is a multilateral network designed to remove friction and time spent on cross‑border corporate payments by facilitating transactions from the bank of origin directly to the beneficiary bank. It increases visibility into the transaction flow between participants, enables tracking of payment status in near real time, and can also support transactions to non‑participating banks. It is described as a closed, permissioned network with Digital ID and direct messaging within the network to support case resolution.

Enables predictable, secure and cost‑effective cross‑border B2B payments for financial institutions and their corporate clients by improving visibility and tracking of payments (near real time), supporting same‑day or next business day full‑value delivery to the beneficiary bank (for participating flows), providing clearer costs and schedules to reduce uncertainty and aid reconciliation, and offering enhanced data (direct messaging) for efficient case resolution.

Type of Fee: Regular

Frequency: Monthly

Visa Chip Authenticate is a value‑added EMV service that validates chip cryptograms on behalf of issuers, enabling them to quickly and cost-effectively adopt and maintain contact and contactless chip capabilities. The service provides flexibility to remove chip data fields from authorization messages as needed, streamlining the processing environment.

Reduces counterfeit fraud risk and improves authorization outcomes by validating the unique EMV chip cryptogram generated for each transaction on behalf of the issuer. It continuously updates to support new cryptogram versions and emerging security needs, significantly reducing the issuer's operational burden and costs associated with manual validation.

Standard Visa monthly invoices are generated on the 4th business day of each month.  Invoice package is available to view and download on Visa Online Invoice Portal (VOIP).  Visa requires all U.S. licensees and processors, including processor independent sales organizations (ISOs), to have an automated collection method set up to pay their Visa invoices by electing one of the following automated payment options:

A valid 6 digits settlement entity ID (formerly known as Settlement Bank Identification Number)

A valid Automated Clearing House (ACH) account

Brazil Payment Instructions:

Fees owed by Brazilian clients as a result of their participation in the Visa Payment Arrangements (the "Domestic Fees") shall be paid in Brazilian reals (BRL) to VISA DO BRASIL EMPREENDIMENTOS LTDA. For that purpose, all references in this Brazil Fee Schedule to a currency other than the Brazilian real shall be interpreted only as reference for fees calculation.

Domestic fees shall be converted into reals in accordance with the Visa Annual Exchange Rate. Visa will base the annual exchange rate on a calculation of the 12-month simple average of the forward rate disclosed by Bloomberg on the last business day of each calendar year. The rate will remain fixed from 1 January through 31 December of each year. For 2023, the Visa Annual Exchange Rate is BRL 5.486642

To avoid any doubt, the Visa Annual Exchange Rate will be used for the purposes of any invoice issued by Visa do Brasil Empreendimentos LTDA during the period covered by the respective rate.

International processing fees (i.e., ad valorem base as defined in the Visa Fee Schedule) will not be subject to the Visa Annual Exchange Rate, and will be converted to reals in accordance with the BASE II rates from the last Central Processing Date (CPD) of the previous month. Clients may access the BASE II rates (purchase or sale) by accessing the TC 56 report on VisaNet.

The billing and payment method will be implemented in accordance with information provided by the client in the Information Sheet. The client must ensure that all information is up-to-date prior to the full local billing implementation date, including:

Clients must pay the fees owed on their respective due dates (without any type of withholding or deductions, except those required by Brazilian tax law) in the form of a bank transfer credited immediately to Visa do Brasil's account at the latter's designated financial institution, in accordance with payment instructions.

For assessed fees based on data reported in the Operating Certificate, clients must pay fees by the 10th business day following issuance of the respective invoice by Visa do Brasil. In the first month of the quarter, the bill will include the invoice for one-third of the respective quarterly amount, with the remainder subject to an advance for services for the next two months of the quarter. In each of the two months of the invoice, the issuance by Visa do Brasil will correspond to one-third of the total amount for the quarter, according to the accrual system. For all other fees, payment must be made monthly by the 10th business day following the issuance of the respective invoice by Visa do Brasil.

Outstanding or unpaid amounts will be subject to a penalty for late payment equivalent to 2% of the amount owed, adjusted in accordance with the variation of the IGP-M / FGV inflation index or any index that may replace it, plus interest of one percent per month, as calculated on a daily basis.

Visa Fees

The document entitled Visa Fee Guide establishes the fees and penalties applicable to Participants in the Visa Payment Schemes. To access and use Visa products and services, the Participant must pay the corresponding fees, as established or periodically revised by Visa.

The Visa Fee Guide is an integral part of the Visa Payment Schemes Regulations implemented in Brazil (“Regulations”) and sets forth:
(i) the Fees and other forms of remuneration (Regular and Eventual) and their respective calculation methodologies; and
(ii) the penalties applicable to Participants, indicating the triggering events.

The information contained in the Visa Fee Guide is proprietary and is intended exclusively for use by Participants in the Visa Payment Schemes. The reproduction, publication, or disclosure of this information, in whole or in part, without Visa’s prior and express written authorization, is prohibited.

The provisions of the Visa Fee Guide apply to all Participants in the Visa Payment Schemes in Brazil, according to their respective participation modality, without prejudice to additional obligations set forth in the Regulations, in specific agreements entered into with Visa, or in applicable laws and regulations.

The information contained in the Visa Fee Guide may be amended periodically. Participants are advised to contact their Visa representative to confirm the effectiveness and applicability of the information.

Classification

Governance, Publication, and Versions of the Guide

The Visa Fee Guide will be made available to Participants through Visa’s official channels, which constitute the formal and binding means of disclosure of applicable fees, penalties, and their respective conditions.

Visa will always make the current version of the Guide available, clearly indicating its effective start date, and may carry out periodic updates in accordance with applicable regulations.

Changes involving the creation of new fees or penalties, or increases to existing amounts, will be disclosed with reasonable prior notice, except when resulting from subsequent legal or regulatory requirements.

Consultation of the current versions of the Guide via Visa’s official channels is the Participant’s responsibility, and the fees, penalties, and conditions set forth therein shall be deemed known and accepted as of their effective date.

Invoices

Visa’s standard monthly invoices are issued on the fourth business day of each calendar month. The set of invoices is available for review and download on the Visa Online Invoice Portal (VOIP).

Payment Instructions in Brazil

Regular and Eventual Fees associated with transactions carried out under Visa Domestic Payment Schemes (“Domestic Fees”) must be paid in Brazilian reais (BRL) to Visa do Brasil Empreendimentos Ltda. (“Visa”). When established as fixed amounts, they will be priced in BRL.

Penalties must be paid in BRL to Visa do Brasil Empreendimentos Ltda. (“Visa”).

Regular and Eventual Fees associated with transactions carried out under Visa International (or Cross-Border) Payment Schemes (“International Fees”) must be paid in BRL to Visa do Brasil Empreendimentos Ltda. (“Visa”). When established as fixed amounts, they will be priced in U.S. dollars (USD) and converted into BRL based on the BASE II exchange rates of the last Central Processing Date (CPD) of the preceding month.

The Regular International Processing Fee, established on an ad valorem basis as provided in the Visa Fee Guide, is not subject to Visa’s Annual Exchange Rate and will be converted into BRL in accordance with the BASE II rates of the last Central Processing Date (CPD) of the month immediately preceding billing. The applicable BASE II rates (buying or selling, as applicable) may be consulted by Members through the TC56 report available on VisaNet.

Billing and payment methods will be implemented based on the information provided by the Participant in the Information Form, a registration document through which the Participant provides Visa with the data required for billing, collection, and compliance with legal and regulatory obligations. The Participant is responsible for ensuring such information is complete, accurate, and kept up to date, including but not limited to:

  • Legal Name
  • National Registry of Legal Entities (CNPJ)
  • Address
  • Contact information

Payment of Fees and Penalties must be made on their respective due dates, without withholdings or deductions, except those required by Brazilian tax law, by means of a bank transfer with immediate credit to the account held by Visa at the financial institution designated by it, in accordance with applicable payment instructions.

Fees calculated based on information contained in the Operational Certificate must be paid by the 10th (tenth) business day following issuance of the respective invoice by Visa. In the first month of each quarter, the invoice will correspond to one-third of the quarterly amount due, plus an advance related to services for the following two months. In each of the subsequent two months, an additional one-third of the total quarterly amount will be invoiced, in accordance with the accrual basis.

All other Fees must be paid monthly, by the 10th business day following issuance of the respective invoice.

Late Payment

Overdue and unpaid amounts will be subject to a late payment penalty of 2% (two percent) on the amount due, adjusted by the variation of the IGP-M/FGV index, or another official index that may replace it, plus default interest of 1% (one percent) per month, calculated pro rata die, without prejudice to other measures provided in the Regulations.

Adjustment of Fees and Penalties

Fees and Penalties may be adjusted annually to preserve their real value. The adjustment will be calculated based on the accumulated variation of the Broad Consumer Price Index (IPCA), published by the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE), measured over the 12 (twelve) months immediately preceding the adjustment base date, and applied annually in March.

In the event the IPCA is discontinued, replaced, or becomes unavailable, another official index that adequately reflects changes in purchasing power will be adopted, observing the same periodicity and reference period.

Such adjustments will not require a formal amendment to the Regulations, and updated values will be disclosed to Participants through Visa’s official channels, in compliance with applicable regulations.

Taxes

All amounts owed by Participants to Visa do not include any taxes, fees, contributions, surcharges, or charges, including, without limitation, taxes on value added, sales, use, consumption, goods and services, equalization taxes, withholding taxes, digital services taxes, or any other taxes levied on Visa’s gross revenue.

Visa may charge the Participant for any taxes it is legally required to collect or declare, in addition to the originally due amounts, upon presentation of an invoice or tax document that meets applicable legal requirements, when required.

If, under applicable law, the Participant is required to withhold, deduct, or collect taxes on payments made to Visa or related to goods or services provided by Visa, the amounts payable to Visa shall be grossed up so that Visa receives the same net amount it would have received had no withholding occurred.

For clarity, the Participant is fully responsible for complying with its tax obligations under applicable law. When applicable, the Participant will act as Visa’s withholding agent or tax responsible party with respect to taxes levied on Visa Fees, and must remit such taxes to the appropriate authorities and promptly provide Visa with the official proof of payment.

The Participant shall indemnify or reimburse Visa for any interest, fines, penalties, or similar charges imposed on Visa as a result of the Participant’s failure to comply with such obligations or that would not have been imposed had such obligations been properly fulfilled.

Information regarding Visa Fees may be updated periodically. Current versions will be made available through Visa’s official channels, and Participants are advised to consult such channels to confirm applicable conditions.

Fees Associated with Services Outside the Payment Schemes

Notwithstanding their inclusion in the Visa Fee Guide, certain services occasionally offered by Visa to Participants may fall outside the scope of the Visa Payment Scheme when they cumulatively meet the objective criteria established in this section and do not affect the operation, authorization, settlement, or governance of the Scheme.

For purposes of the Visa Fee Guide, a charge will be deemed related to a service outside the Payment Scheme when all of the following conditions are met:

(i) the service is not essential to the operation of the Payment Scheme and does not constitute a condition for participation, continued participation, or activity within the Scheme;
(ii) the service is not provided by Visa in its capacity as Payment Scheme Operator and may be offered by third parties;
(iii) the service is contracted separately, optionally, and independently, and is not imposed as a regulatory, operational, or contractual requirement for access to the Scheme’s functionalities;
(iv) the service does not directly affect authorization, clearing, settlement, or fund transfers related to transactions processed within the Scheme;
(v) the pricing of the service is not linked to the volume, value, or number of transactions processed within the Payment Scheme, except where such linkage is objectively justified by the specific and independent cost of the service, in which case the calculation methodology must be expressly indicated.

Without prejudice to their non-Scheme nature, fees related to such services will be disclosed to Participants in advance in a clear and transparent manner and will remain subject to the provisions above, particularly with respect to payment instructions, late payment, adjustments, and taxes, in order to avoid informational asymmetries and in accordance with the principles of transparency and predictability.

f.h:
Visa Resolve Online (VROL) is a global dispute processing platform that enables issuers and acquirers to process disputes within their front-line or back-office workflows (from inquiry/pre-dispute through pre-filing and case filing, including arbitration and compliance)

VROL provides a standardized and electronic process for submitting, validating, and managing disputes, helping improve efficiency and consistency across the ecosystem. By applying validation edits and structured workflows, it helps reduce invalid or incomplete disputes and supports faster resolution. This contributes to clearer collaboration between issuers, acquirers, and Visa, and more predictable dispute outcomes. With Visa Resolve Online, issuers can manage dispute processing faster and more efficiently to save time and money

Type of fee: Regular

Billing Frequency: Monthly

Note: 

  1. For Tiered pricing, it is the date on which a questionnaire is received (receipt date, system GMT) and when a response questionnaire is submitted.
  2. Financial submissions may take up to 48 hours from the receipt date to settle with Visa.
  3. VROL fees apply to all VROL activity for Visa, Interlink, Plus and all other network or transactions.

f.h:
Visa Credential Enrichment Service (VCES) enhances token provisioning by using VisaNet data to identify the latest confirmed expiry date associated with a PAN and, where available, swaps in the newer expiry date so stored credentials with outdated expiry dates can be used to provision tokens. For eligible token provisioning requests with outdated or absent PAN expiration dates, VCES updates the PAN expiry date within the provisioning request; a charge is assessed only when VCES performs an expiry-date update and the token is successfully provisioned. No implementation or technical changes are required to use the service, as it is managed by Visa. Improves token provisioning success for eCommerce and Card‑on‑File (COF) use cases by enriching eligible provisioning requests with the most up‑to‑date PAN expiry date available in VisaNet, helping reduce false provisioning declines and improve approval rates for recurring payments, without requiring technical/integration changes for participants.

"Service Not Included in Visa’s Payment Arrangements"

f.p: Visa Dispute Management Service - Global Standard
f.n: Visa Dispute Management Services Case Fee
f.h:
Visa Dispute Management Service (VDMS) - Global Standard is an on-behalf-of dispute case management solution. After the issuer or fintech accepts the initial dispute from the cardholder, Visa manages the entire back-end dispute lifecycle through completion. This includes handling case review, chargebacks, merchant response evaluation, pre-arbitration, and arbitration. Allows issuers and eligible fintechs to maintain the direct relationship with their cardholders while outsourcing back-end dispute processing to Visa. This shared-service solution helps optimize recovery rates, ensure rule compliance, and significantly reduce internal operational workload and costs. 

Type of Fee: Regular

Billing Frequency Monthly

f.h:
Visa Processing Performance Monitor (VPPM) provides near real time information, related to the performance of the Visa transactions processing through Visa’s network.

f.h:
Visa Sensitive Data Protection (SDP) is a value-added service that obfuscates sensitive cardholder information and removes Track II data (if present) for issuers during authorization, clearing, and settlement. The service applies to selected V.I.P. messages and SMS Raw Data files, seamlessly replacing the obfuscated PAN with the real PAN in responses returned to the acquirer. Helps issuers and issuer processors reduce the effort and cost of protecting sensitive payment data by obfuscating the Primary Account Number (PAN) and removing certain personal information before the data reaches the client's environment. This simplifies PCI DSS compliance and helps eliminate the need to procure, operate, and maintain Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) for data encryption. 

Type of Fee: Regular

Billing Frequency Monthly

The Visa Sensitive Data Protection service allows new cloud-based fintechs, neo-banks and issuers to begin processing more quickly and Visa Sensitive Data Protection can potentially remove the need to deploy costly Payment Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) and their associated secure datacenter infrastructure if the client subscribes to Visa's On-Behalf-Of HSM services. This service can also help significantly reduce the amount of work required to achieve Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) compliance and allows data to be stored as-is without the need for additional development to securely encrypt the data.

Visa Stop Payment Service (VSPS) is a value-added service that allows issuers to create and manage “stop instructions” to block future unwanted payments before they are authorized and completed. The service is available via Visa Access and through a suite of APIs on the Visa Developer platform.  VSPS supports searching eligible transactions and creating, updating, extending, or canceling stop instructions, with automated features designed to help reduce duplicate instructions and manage active stops over time.Helps issuers stop unwanted future card-not-present payments from debiting a cardholder’s account. It reduces customer service calls and disputes tied to recurring or unrecognized payments while giving cardholders more control over their subscriptions, which can support long-term retention.

Visa Accelerated Connection Platform (ACP) is a connectivity solution that enables participating clients to route authorization transactions through a direct interface to VisaNet. The platform is designed to support common front-end processing connectivity for merchants, acquirers, and integrators, and may also support additional transaction routing capabilities where available. Helps streamline front-end payment connectivity by providing a direct interface into VisaNet for multinational integrators, acquirers, and merchants. This supports more consistent point-of-sale integration and enables payment processing across markets through a common connection framework. 

Type of Fee:Regular

Billing Frequency Monthly

ACP pricing applies to any transaction delivered to Visa by a participating merchant via the ACP interface. All charges are billed to the merchant's acquiring sponsor.

To mitigate this, the On Behalf of Issuer Lifecycle Manager (OBO LCM) will update expired Primary Account Numbers (PANs) and associated expired card-on-file or eCommerce tokens on behalf of issuers. This service aims to increase card-not-present authorization rates where Visa can access valid(newer) card expiry dates, thereby enhancing the overall e-commerce user experience by reducing out-of-date credential declines.

The Non-compliance Assessments section specifies assessments applicable to acquirers, issuers and processors.

The Visa Rules contain enforcement mechanisms that Visa may use for violations of the Visa Rules. The Visa Rules specify the procedure for the allegation and investigation of violations and the rules and schedules for non-compliance assessments.

A client that does not comply with the Visa Rules will be subject to non-compliance assessments.

These procedures and non-compliance assessments are in addition to enforcement rights available to Visa under other provisions of the Visa Rules, or through other legal or administrative procedures.

The Non-compliance Assessments section includes information on:

  • General Non-compliance Assessments
  • Significant Violation of Non-compliance Assessments
  • Issuer Non-compliance Assessments
  • Acquirer Non-compliance Assessments
  • Issuer / Acquirer Non-compliance Assessments

If you have questions or need additional information, please contact your Visa account executive.

By proceeding, users consent to abide by the Visa Non-Disclosure Agreement.

Inspections—Client and Agent Facilities

  • Refer to the Inspections—Client and Agent Facilities page in the Visa Assessed Fees for the Acquirer Monitor Program non-compliance penalty fee.

High-Risk Internet Payment Facilitators

An acquirer that fails to comply with the registration program requirements for high-risk internet payment facilitators, as specified in the Visa Rules, is subject to non-compliance assessments.

  • For the specific schedule amounts, please refer to the section in the Visa Rules under Rule ID #0026334.

Visa Dispute Monitoring Program - Ends 31 March 2025

Visa assesses Visa Dispute Monitoring Program (VDMP) fees and non-compliance assessments to the Acquirer, as specified in the Visa Rules.

  • For the specific schedule amounts, please refer to the section in the Visa Rules under Rule ID #0029291

Data Quality Non-compliance Assessments

If Visa determines that an acquirer or merchant changed, modified or altered the merchant name or merchant data in any way to circumvent the Visa Dispute Monitoring Program, Visa may charge a monthly non-compliance assessment to the acquirer for each merchant outlet.

  • For the specific schedule amounts, please refer to the section in the Visa Rules under Rule ID #0030702.

Visa Acquirer Monitoring Program  - Ends 31 March 2025

Visa assesses non-compliance assessments if an acquirer’s monthly card-absent environment dispute or card-absent environment fraud activity, or monthly enumeration attack activity, meets or exceeds the Visa Acquirer Monitoring Program (VAMP) thresholds, as specified in the Visa Rules.

  • For the specific schedule amounts, please refer to the section in the Visa Rules under Rule ID #0029293.

Visa Fraud Monitoring Program - Ends 31 March 2025

The acquirer of a merchant outlet identified in the Visa Fraud Monitoring Program (VFMP) is subject to non-compliance assessments under either the standard or high-risk/excessive timelines, as specified in the Visa Rules.

  • For the specific schedule amounts, please refer to the section in the Visa Rules under Rule ID #0029294.

Non-compliance Assessments for Failure to Report Fraud

An issuer that does not comply with the Fraud Reporting Program's requirements, as determined by the third or higher consecutive onsite audit, will be subject to a quarterly non-compliance assessment until found compliant by the Visa remote monitoring system and validated by an onsite audit.

  • For the specific schedule amounts, please refer to the section in the Visa Rules under Rule ID #0028308.Information in the Non-compliance Assessments section may change from time to time. Please contact your Visa representative to verify current information. Visa is not responsible for errors in this publication.

Authorization Requests for Online Gambling Transactions

An acquirer is subject to the fees specified below if an authorization request for an online gambling transaction contains incorrect data.

1 All violations must be corrected within seven days of notification. Correction of the violation does not eliminate the fee liability.
2 These fees are adjusted to better reflect market conditions.

Online Gambling Credit Compliance Program

An acquirer is subject to the fees specified below for an online gambling merchant in the Online Gambling Credit Compliance Program.

E-commerce Merchant Monitoring Program

An acquirer is subject to the fees specified below if it fails to terminate a merchant, internet payment service provider (IPSP), or sponsored merchant that displays a Visa-owned mark on its website or accepts cards for the purchase or trade of child pornography.

Validation Requirements 

If an acquirer client, its merchants, or service providers do not comply with the Account Information Security (AIS) Program requirements, the client is responsible for the following fee.

Information Compromise

Acquirer clients that are not in compliance with the Account Information Security (AIS) Program at the moment of an incident are subject to the following fee.

Compromise Incident Notification Requirements

A client that does not report the loss or theft of information is subject to a fee per incident.

Prohibited Data Storage

A client or a client's merchant or agent, deemed as non-compliant with the Account Information Security (AIS) Program may be subject to the following fees.

Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS) 

Visa will impose fees to acquirers that fail to provide an attestation form to Visa confirming that each of its level 1 merchants has validated Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS) compliance.

Cross-Border Illegal Transactions

Visa acquirers and merchants currently must not process illegal transactions in the Visa payment system, as specified in the Visa Rules. Transactions determined to be illegal in either the buyer's or seller's jurisdiction are prohibited from entering the Visa system: Visa will notify affected clients of such prohibited transactions in the Visa system.

An acquirer is subject to the following fees if it fails to take actions against a merchant identified as processing illegal cross-border transactions:

High-Risk E-commerce Merchant Monitoring Standards

Visa may impose security or authentication requirements on a merchant considered to be a high-risk e-commerce merchant. If the risk control measures specified in the Visa Rules are not implemented, the acquirer will be subject to a monthly fee until remediation occurs.

Incorrect Use of E-commerce Transaction Indicator Values

An acquirer is subject to the fees specified below if an e-commerce transaction is not identified with the correct e-commerce transaction indicator values.

Visa Integrity Risk Program

An acquirer that processes illegal or prohibited transactions, as specified in the Visa Rules, is subject to non-compliance assessments.

  • For the specific schedule amounts, please refer to the section in the Visa Rules under Rule ID #0026387.

ATM Access Fee

Visa adds an ATM special handling fee to acquirers on international ATM transactions that are not submitted for CPS / ATM or fail the CPS / ATM edit criteria.

Account Information Security Program

A client deemed non-compliant with the Account Information Security (AIS) Program, as specified in the Visa Rules, is subject to non-compliance Assessments.

  • For the specific schedule amounts, please refer to the section in the Visa Rules under Rule ID #0008193 and the Account Information Security (AIS) Program Guide (PDF).

Information in the Non-compliance Assessments section may change from time to time. Please contact your Visa representative to verify current information. Visa is not responsible for errors in this publication.

Data Quality Non-compliance Assessments
If Visa determines that an acquirer or merchant changed, modified or altered the merchant name or merchant data in any way to circumvent the Visa Dispute Monitoring Program, Visa may charge a monthly non-compliance assessment to the acquirer for each merchant outlet.
For the specific schedule amounts, please refer to the section in the Visa Rules under Rule ID #0030702.
Visa Acquirer Monitoring Program - Ends 31 March 2025
Visa assesses non-compliance assessments if an acquirer’s monthly card-absent environment dispute or card-absent environment fraud activity, or monthly enumeration attack activity, meets or exceeds the Visa Acquirer Monitoring Program (VAMP) thresholds, as specified in the Visa Rules.
For the specific schedule amounts, please refer to the section in the Visa Rules under Rule ID #0029293.
Visa Fraud Monitoring Program - Ends 31 March 2025

For the specific schedule amounts, please refer to the section in the Visa Rules under Rule ID #0029294.

ATM Excessive Denial Fee

Visa assesses an issuer an ATM excessive denial fee of USD 5 for each declined transaction below the minimum approval rate of 65 percent. This fee excludes transactions receiving the following response codes:

For deposit access transactions (debit and prepaid):

  • 04 – Pick-up Card
  • 07 – Pick-up Card, Special Condition
  • 41 – Pick-up Card, Lost
  • 43 – Pick-up Card, Stolen
  • 51 – Not Sufficient Funds

For all other transactions:

  • 04 – Pick-up Card
  • 05 – Do not Honor
  • 07 – Pick-up Card, Special Condition
  • 41 – Pick-up Card, Lost
  • 43 – Pick-up Card, Stolen

 

Failure to Issue PINs

If an issuer fails to issue PINs to its cardholders, the issuer is subject to a fee per outstanding Visa card and Visa Electron card, as reported on this Quarterly Operating Certificate.

Excessive Decline Rates

An issuer that fails to comply with the criteria specified in “Decline Response Prohibition for Electronic Commerce Transactions,” as specified in the Visa Rules, Interlink Rules or Plus Rules, is subject to non-compliance assessments.

ATM Excessive Denial Fee

Visa assesses an issuer an ATM excessive denial fee of USD 5 for each declined transaction below the minimum approval rate of 65 percent. This fee excludes transactions receiving the following response codes:

For deposit access transactions (debit and prepaid):

  • 04 – Pick-up Card
  • 07 – Pick-up Card, Special Condition
  • 41 – Pick-up Card, Lost
  • 43 – Pick-up Card, Stolen

For all other transactions:

  • 04 – Pick-up Card
  • 05 – Do not Honor
  • 07 – Pick-up Card, Special Condition
  • 41 – Pick-up Card, Lost
  • 43 – Pick-up Card, Stolen

 

Failure to Issue PINs

If an issuer fails to issue PINs to its cardholders, the issuer is subject to a fee per outstanding Visa card and Visa Electron card, as reported on this Quarterly Operating Certificate.

Excessive Decline Rates

An issuer that fails to comply with the criteria specified in “Decline Response Prohibition for Electronic Commerce Transactions,” as specified in the Visa Rules, Interlink Rules or Plus Rules, is subject to non-compliance assessments.

Fraud Reporting System

  • For the specific schedule amounts, please refer to the section in the Visa Rules under Rule ID #0028308.Information in the Non-compliance Assessments section may change from time to time. Please contact your Visa representative to verify current information. Visa is not responsible for errors in this publication.

Visa Signature Authorization Standards

A Visa Signature issuer that exceeds the Negative Authorization Response3 standard of two percent, as a percentage of its total Authorization Responses in a calendar month, is subject to a fee for each Negative Authorization Response3 Fee exceeding the standard.

3 A Negative Response Authorization is any authorization response that is not an approval.

Fee for Client Failure to Report Fraud

A client that does not comply with the "Fraud Activity Reporting" and "Fraud Activity Reporting Time Limit," as specified in the Visa Rules, is subject to an onsite audit by Visa staff at the client's expense and non-compliance assessments as specified in the Visa Rules.

A client must pay a Settlement Late Payment Fee if a settlement amount is not transferred by the required date. The Settlement Late Payment Fee is computed on the following basis, subject to a minimum of $500 per calendar day.

Calculation

The Settlement Late Payment Fee is calculated as follows:

  • Calendar days include the day the settlement amount is due and excludes the day the settlement amount is correctly transferred.
  • Prime Rate is the rate in effect at the Visa settlement bank on the day the funds are correctly transferred.

Minimum Settlement Late Payment Fee

Information in the Visa Assessed Fees section may change from time to time. Please contact your Visa representative to verify current information. Visa is not responsible for errors in this publication.

b.inv: VISA CREDENTIAL ENRICHMENT SERVICE - TOKEN PROVISION EXPIRY ENHANCEMENT
b.ld: Visa Credential Enrichment Service (VCES) supports Token Requestors in provisioning Tokens for their stored & validated PAN credentials, in cases where the PAN expiration date of the credential is no longer up-to-date/available. The Service maintains a mapping of PANs to Expiry Dates used in VisaNet Card-Present, Approved Chip txns, and utilizes this mapping to assist in creation of Tokens for eligible requests. For eligible Token provision requests with outdated/absent PAN expiration dates, the VCES service updates the PAN expiry date associated with credential within the provision request. Charge is assessed for each VCES-updated request resulting in a successfully provisioned Token

b.ld: Issuers are sometimes unable to update credentials due to various reasons, leading to declined transactions, cardholder friction, and potential non-compliance penalties. To mitigate this, the Issuer OBO Credential Update Service will update expired Primary Account Numbers (PANs) and associated expired card-on-file or eCommerce tokens on behalf of issuers. This service aims to increase card-not-present authorization rates where Visa can access valid(newer) card expiry dates, thereby enhancing the overall e-commerce user experience by reducing out-of-date credential declines.
b.ct: Acquirer, Acquirer Processor, Issuer, Issuer Processor

b.inv: TOKEN LIFECYCLE MANAGEMENT (TLCM) TOOL SUBSCRIPTION FEE
b.ld: The Token Lifecycle Management (TLCM) tool is a web-based application provided by Visa, accessible via the Visa Online (VOL) platform. This tool allows issuers to manually update token states and credentials. It is an integral part of the Visa Tokenization Program and is available to all active and basic issuers participating in the program. The tool serves as an alternative to the Lifecycle Management (LCM) APIs and ISO messages, which provide automatic updates to token states and credentials. While these automated options are available, there have been instances where issuers have not been able to update consistently or correctly using the Visa Token Service (VTS) LCM APIs. The TLCM tool thus serves as an essential component in maintaining token lifecycle management events, contributing to improved authorization approval performance and enhancing the cardholder experience. However, it's important to note that there are costs associated with maintaining the TLCM application each year, which Visa intends to recover.
b.ct: Issuer, Issuer Processor
b.pr: Token Lifecycle Management (TLCM) Subscription Fee | BRL 3.234

pd.d: The Visa Authorization Gateway allows acquirers and processors to link to a wider network of payment card brands through their VisaNet connection. This provides clients the flexibility of using the Visa message format to send authorization messages for the following networks: Mastercard, American Express, Discover, Diners, and JCB.

Visa Account Name Inquiry is a service that allows card-not-present merchants to validate a customer’s name against the issuer’s system before initiating a transaction. The merchant sends the cardholder’s full name through an account verification message. The message responds with a code that identifies whether the name matches, partially matches or doesn’t match the issuer’s payment account data. Visa Account Name Inquiry gives issuers and merchants a tool for reducing fraud and authorized push payment scams.

Account Verification is an online message used to confirm the validity of a cardholder’s account. Account Verification uses zero-value authorization to ensure an account is valid and in good standing according to the issuer. Clients get access to quick, accurate and secure account validation that streamlines the authorization process.

Visa Resolve Online (VROL) is a global platform that enables issuers and acquirers to process disputes within their front-line or back-office workflows. Visa Resolve Online features a modernized, updated dispute process that automates and streamlines the entire dispute process. With Visa Resolve Online, issuers can manage dispute processing faster and more efficiently to save time and money.

The Global Client Testing Services support client testing activities associated with new implementations, system changes, or updates within the payment processing environment.

Access to testing support that helps reduce operational risk and supports readiness for live payment processing activities.

Fee type: Occasional/Optional

Licensing services consist of the granting of rights to use Visa intellectual property, trademarks, technology, and related services in connection with payment products and programs, subject to applicable terms and conditions.

Access to licensed functionality that supports participation in Visa programs and the use of Visa intellectual property.

Fee type: Regular

Client Directory enables clients to access and maintain service provider and operational contact information associated with issuing BINs and Acquiring IDs. The directory supports operational coordination, incident management, and required communications in accordance with Visa Rules.

The client obtains access to the Client Directory, which provides centralized contact and service provider information associated with issuing Bank Identification Numbers (BINs) and Acquiring IDs to support client‑to‑client and Visa‑to‑client operational communications.

Fee type: Regular Optional

Visa Chip Authenticate is an EMV solution that quickly and cost-effectively gives issuers chip payment capabilities. Chip Authenticate validates the unique code generated by each chip payment on behalf of issuers, and the solution automatically updates to keep pace with new security technologies. Because Chip Authenticate takes on code validation, issuers save the time and money they would otherwise spend on manual validation.

Dynamic Cardholder Verification Value 2 (dCCV2) is a three-digit code that replaces the existing CVV. Consumers can use this dynamic code to make secure purchases at merchants’ point-of-sale systems. There are three dCCV2 services available to issuers: dCCV2 Generate, which allows issuers to call Visa to obtain a code, dCCV2 Authenticate, which validates codes on behalf of issuers, and dCCV2 Convert, which replaces the code with a static value. Because dynamic data is far less vulnerable to fraud, this service gives issuers an opportunity to boost the cardholder experience, while allowing cardholders to make secure, confident purchases.

Edit Package is a service that validates clearing records on behalf of Visa clients. The service also provides access to BIN-specific data and exception records. With Edit Package, clients get quick, accurate record validation and file management.

pd.p: Hardware Security Module as a Service
pd.d: HSM-As-A-Service pallows Visa to provide full payment cryptographic functions on-behlaf-of clients so that clients do not need to have their own payment Hardware Security Modules (HSM) and related costly infrastructure to support payment cryptographic functions. This service is available for Issuers and Issuer Processors. ** Note: It is presumed that clients will use a 3rd party Card Personalization Bureau for card generation and personalization, as a HSM is required for the process.

The Visa Merchant Search API makes it easier for cardholders to recognize transactions. Merchant Search API helps you cleanse and enrich merchant data — providing your cardholders with clear, easy-to-understand information for each transaction, which may include merchant name, location, phone number, and URL. This enhanced transaction information can help you reduce cardholder transaction inquiries, improve cardholder experience, and strengthen cardholder loyalty.

Network Direct Peering is a service that allows clients that have infrastructure hosted at Equinix or are connected to Equinix to be able to directly peer with Visa’s infrastructure on Equinix to connect to selected VisaNet services for API based message traffic. This service provides a more robust and resilient connection compared to over the Internet based connectivity. This service is available to Issuers, Acquirers and Processors.

The Push Payment Gateway facilitates both original credit and account funding transactions from non-Visa networks. The solution provides access to send payments or request funding through other networks via any VisaNet connection including the Visa Direct’s APIs. This service is currently available for acquirers on regional networks such as Maestro (MoneySend), STAR, NYCE and Pulse.

VIP System Reporting provide issuers with authorization reports. Reports include data on authorization profiles, cardholder databases, card verification values and custom payment services. These VIP reports give issuers key insights into authorization performance and accounts listed in Visa Account Screen via the file format that best meets their needs.

Visa Analytics Platform is a web-based, self-service analytics solution that empowers organizations (for example, issuers, acquirers, and co-brands) to gain actionable payments intelligence — helping them make faster, more informed business decisions. With powerful peer benchmarking*, easy-to-understand dashboards, and customizable reports, organizations can use Visa Analytics Platform to help improve portfolio performance, increase cardholder engagement, reduce fraud and declines, understand merchant performance, lower disputes, and more.*Peer benchmarking data is currently available only to Issuers.

Visa Card Enrollment Hub (VCEH) is a service that enables cardholders to use their banking application to easily enroll their payment credentials to a merchant account. By eliminating the need for cardholders to manually input their card and personal information, VCEH allows consumers to quickly and securely enroll in subscriptions, retail accounts and more. VCEH gives merchants the opportunity to provide a better and more streamlined cardholder onboarding experience, thus driving payment volume and top-of-wallet status.

Visa Cloud Connect can enable financial instutitions, processors and approved third parties to connect to VisaNet via a cloud-based infrastructure. With Visa Cloud Connect, clients get the option to set up a virtual private cloud infrastructure with a supported cloud provider of their choosing, enabling straightforward and flexible access to VisaNet. Seamless access to VisaNet enables financial institutions to gain more efficient card transaction acceptance, authorization and clearing.

Visa Credential Enrichment Service (VCES) is a service that enables merchants and digital partners to provision tokens to stored cardholder credentials with expired dates. VCES uses VisaNet data to identify the latest confirmed date associated with the cardholder’s PAN. It then swaps in the newer expiry date where available. With VCES, merchant, digital partners and issuers get access to an enhanced token provisioning process that improves the cardholder experience.

Visa Dedicated Access is a service that provides clients with secure and reliable direct connections to VisaNet. The service uses direct exchange, extended access server or extended access proxy at the client datacenters to connect into VisaNet via leased line circuits. With Visa Dedicated Access, clients can get dependable and high-availability connections to the Visa’s electronic payment network.

The Visa Digital Enablement (VDE) SDK enables clients to deliver compelling cardholder experiences through an easy to implement, configurable suite of an ever-growing feature set that simplifies the development process by enabling multiple connections, thereby accelerating market entry, and reducing the cost and complexity of directly interfacing with various endpoints into a common connection.

pd.p: Visa Dispute Management Service - Global Standard
pd.d: Visa Dispute Management Services is a solution that manages dispute resolution on behalf of issuers who do not process wtih DPS. Visa Dispute Management Services handles all back-end dispute processing, while enabling issuers to accept payment disputes and maintain connection with their cardholders. By outsourcing dispute resolution, issuers can achieve higher recovery rates and potentially reduce operational expenses.

The Visa File Exchange Service provides clients with internet-based file transfers to/from Visa. This service is designed for issuers, acquirers and processors. With Visa File Exchange Service, clients can transfer VisaNet files quickly and seamlessly directly through their account.

Visa Processing Performance Monitor (VPPM) provides information related to the performance of the Visa transactions processing through Visa’s network. VPPM allows Issuer clients to monitor their approval rates and quickly identify early outage events or any unexpected changes in their portfolio behavior.

Visa Sensitive Data Protection is a service that provides masking of PAI and PII data in the full financial authorization message and in the SMS Raw Data files. This service can help meet one of the PCIDSS requirements (encrypted data at rest) that clients have to achieve in order to process payments. This service is for Issuers and Issuer Processors Only.

Visa Stop Payment Service is a value-add service that enables issuers to stop payments before a transaction is authorized and completed. This service is available through Visa Access or as a set of APIs on Visa Developer. It is also part of the Visa Subscription Manager API solution, bundled with the Card on File Data API. With Visa Stop Payment Service, issuers can quickly and easily stop unwanted future CNP payments from debiting a cardholder’s account.

Visa Token Service (VTS) is a payment platform that replaces PANs with tokens, making the payment ecosystem and each token-enhanced transaction more secure. Visa has enabled 198 markets, 8,400 issuers and 2.9m merchants with tokenization capabilities, driving more than 14 billion tokenized transactions worldwide in the most recent quarter. VTS not only gives cardholders a more secure transaction for ecommerce and in-person shopping, but also provides merchants with higher sales, improved authorization rates and stronger authentication processes.

VisaNet Connect APIs offer clients direct access to Visa’s core processing services via an API based interface. The APIs apply to all card-present and card-not-present scenarios and offer an intuitive interface. Through this modern API technology, clients can get easy access to one of the payment processing technologies that powers transactions worldwide.

The client obtains access to clearing and settlement reports generated by Visa systems, which provide aggregated and detailed information on cleared transactions, settlement positions, and funds movement.

pd.cat: Network Fees and VisaNet Processing Charges
pd.d:
Visa Other Miscellaneous Fees apply to select, stand-alone fee items that are assessed under defined circumstances and do not fit neatly within a single product fee group. Examples include fees associated with delivering industry benchmarking reports or related benchmarking services to issuers, fees tied to specific transaction conditions in acceptance flows (e.g., certain contactless transaction handling scenarios), and fees assessed when settlement obligations are not met by required deadlines. These charges are intended to address discrete use cases, operational exceptions, or program-specific conditions rather than ongoing core service usage.

Groups together specific, non-standard charges that support specialized services and operational safeguards across the Visa ecosystem. These fees can cover items such as providing benchmarking and performance insights to help issuers evaluate program results against relevant market references, as well as targeted charges that help reinforce sound payment acceptance practices and reduce avoidable operational risk. In addition, this fee group can include charges that promote timely completion of settlement obligations, helping protect the integrity and reliability of the overall settlement process.

Fee type: Various

Frequency: Various

Fees imposed when a violation of the Visa Rules has occurred or continues to occur, triggered by non‑compliance identified through audits, investigations, or failure to remediate a confirmed issue within the required timeframe.

These assessments help maintain the integrity and proper functioning of the Visa system by addressing instances of non‑compliance and reinforcing adherence to Visa Rules.

Fee type: Penalty/Behavioral

Non‑compliance assessments are applied when a client is identified as not complying with applicable rules, standards, or requirements governing participation in the payment network. The assessments form part of the network’s enforcement framework and may be imposed following notification, investigation, or failure to remediate identified issues, in accordance with established rules and procedures.

By reinforcing compliance obligations, these assessments contribute to consistent operational practices, risk mitigation, and the integrity of the overall ecosystem for all participants.

Fee type: Penalty/Behavioral

The ATM Cash Withdrawal Network is one of the largest systems of ATMs in the world. Cardholders have access to more than 2.6 million ATMs around the globe, each accepting Visa transactions and withdrawals. The ATM Cash Withdrawl Network connects and empowers Visa cardholders, giving them access to cash globally.

Research Services are a suite of information and support tools for Visa clients who are creating new solutions in competitive marketplaces. With staff based around the globe and a 1,500-square-foot Inclusive Research Lab, the Research Services team provides generative research, digital card-sorting techniques and product design ideation and testing. Clients gain data-backed insights that can help them evaluate and refine solutions to ensure they meet—or exceed—users’ expectations.

The Approved Card Vendor Program (AVP) covers the initial review, assessment, and ongoing validation of vendors that provide Visa‑branded card manufacturing, personalization, or fulfillment services. Each card vendor is billed annually dependent on the services they provide to issuers.

It allows vendors to deliver Visa‑branded card manufacturing, personalization, and fulfillment services to issuers while meeting Visa’s security, design, and operational standards, enabling trusted participation in the Visa ecosystem.

Fee type: Occasional

The Third Party Agent Program applies to clients that use third-party agents to perform payment-related services. The program supports the registration, oversight, and ongoing governance of those entities, including client responsibilities for due diligence and compliance with applicable Visa operational and security requirements.
 

Helps protect the Visa ecosystem by ensuring that entities providing payment-related services to Visa clients are registered and aligned with applicable Visa requirements and security standards. It supports stronger third-party oversight and risk management through formal registration and due diligence processes.

Type of Fee: Occasional

Visa Secure enables issuers to authenticate a cardholder’s identity for ecommerce transactions before the transaction is sent for authorization. Visa Secure uses the globally adopted 3-D Secure standard, which provides rules and policies that issuers and merchants must follow when authenticating cardholder data. By using Visa Secure, issuers can enhance the ecommerce shopping experience, reduce unnecessary friction at checkout by expanding data exchanges, and access constantly updating and flexible channel support.
